You are the SVG Diagram Agent for 图研.
Return one standalone, valid SVG document only. Do not use Markdown fences.
Use inline SVG elements such as rect, circle, ellipse, path, line, polyline, polygon, text, defs, marker, linearGradient, and g.
Do not use script, style, foreignObject, image, external URLs, event handlers, JavaScript links, embedded HTML, filters, masks, patterns, group opacity or blending. Use direct geometry, solid fills and gradients; avoid clipping effects.
Use a clean academic diagram style with readable labels, balanced whitespace, and a light background.
Hard renderer contract: no shadows of any kind; never output <filter>, <feDropShadow>, <mask>, <pattern>, <clipPath> or filter=, even inside unused defs. If the supplied plan suggests these effects, replace that styling with flat fills and strokes. Use Noto Sans CJK SC / Noto Sans / Noto Sans Math, regular weight and normal style.
Do not include the figure title or caption text inside the SVG.

Create an editable SVG academic diagram from this visual specification.
Use viewBox="0 0 1600 900" for the requested 16:9 aspect ratio. Keep all artwork within this viewBox.
Prefer simple geometric shapes, arrows, concise labels, and semantic grouping.

Reference image is for design structure only; do not transfer its paper data or conclusions.",

  "completePlan": "Based on the methodology provided and the visual style of the reference image (teal/green palette, white icons/text, clean flat design), here is the detailed description for the illustrative figure.\n\n**Figure Description:**\n\n**Overall Layout and Style:**\nThe image is a vertical flowchart diagram set against a pure white background. The visual style mimics the reference image: it uses a distinct teal-green color (approximate hex #1F8A70) for process blocks and decision points, with white text and icons. The flow moves from top to bottom. All shapes have sharp corners or standard geometric angles (no rounded \"pill\" shapes for start/end, strictly following flowchart conventions). Connecting lines are solid black arrows with standard triangular heads, 2px thickness.\n\n**Elements and Flow (Top to Bottom):**\n\n1.  **Start Node:**\n    *   **Shape:** A stadium shape (rectangle with semi-circular ends), filled with the primary teal-green color.\n    *   **Content:** Centered white text reading **\"Start\"**.\n    *   **Position:** Top center of the canvas.\n    *   **Connection:** A straight black arrow points vertically downward to the next block.\n\n2.  **Process Block 1 (Receive Sample):**\n    *   **Shape:** A standard rectangle with sharp corners, filled with teal-green. Width is approximately 30% of the canvas width.\n    *   **Content:** Centered white text reading **\"Receive sample\"**. To the left of the text, include a simple white line-art icon of a test tube or beaker to match the scientific theme of the reference style.\n    *   **Connection:** A straight black arrow points vertically downward to the decision diamond.\n\n3.  **Decision Node (Quality Check):**\n    *   **Shape:** A diamond (rhombus) shape, filled with teal-green. The width matches the rectangular blocks above.\n    *   **Content:** Centered white text reading **\"Quality check\"**.\n    *   **Connections (Branching):**\n        *   **Yes Branch:** An arrow exits from the **bottom** vertex of the diamond, pointing vertically down. A small label **\"Yes\"** in black text is placed next to the arrow shaft.\n        *   **No Branch:** An arrow exits from the **right** vertex of the diamond, travels horizontally to the right, then turns 90 degrees downward. A small label **\"No\"** in black text is placed next to the horizontal segment.\n\n4.  **Process Block 2 (Normalize - Yes Path):**\n    *   **Shape:** A standard rectangle with sharp corners, filled with teal-green. Aligned directly below the Decision Node.\n    *   **Content:** Centered white text reading **\"Normalize\"**. Include a white line-art icon of a graph or slider to represent adjustment/normalization.\n    *   **Connection:** A straight black arrow points vertically downward to the Output block.\n\n5.  **Process Block 3 (Output - Yes Path):**\n    *   **Shape:** A standard rectangle with sharp corners, filled with teal-green. Aligned directly below the \"Normalize\" block.\n    *   **Content:** Centered white text reading **\"Output\"**. Include a white line-art icon of a document or a tray.\n    *   **Connection:** A straight black arrow points vertically downward to the End node.\n\n6.  **Process Block 4 (Reject Sample - No Path):**\n    *   **Shape:** A standard rectangle with sharp corners, filled with teal-green. Positioned to the right of the main vertical axis, aligned horizontally with the \"Normalize\" block.\n    *   **Content:** Centered white text reading **\"Reject sample\"**. Include a white line-art icon of a trash bin or an \"X\" mark.\n    *   **Connection:** An arrow exits the bottom of this block, travels down, then turns 90 degrees to the left to merge into the final \"End\" node (or simply points to a separate End node if preferred, but merging is cleaner). *Alternative simpler layout:* The arrow points down to its own specific \"End\" terminator located below it. Let's use the specific terminator approach for clarity.\n\n7.  **End Nodes:**\n    *   **Shape:** Stadium shapes (identical to the Start node), filled with teal-green.\n    *   **Content:** Centered white text reading **\"End\"**.\n    *   **Positions:**\n        *   One \"End\" node is located at the very bottom of the central column (connected from \"Output\").\n        *   One \"End\" node is located at the bottom of the right-hand column (connected from \"Reject sample\").\n\n**Typography and Colors:**\n*   **Font:** Sans-serif (e.g., Arial, Helvetica, or Noto Sans), bold weight for legibility.\n*   **Text Color:** Pure White (#FFFFFF) inside the teal blocks; Black (#000000) for branch labels (\"Yes\", \"No\") on the white background.\n*   **Block Color:** Teal Green (matching reference, approx #1F8A70).\n*   **Arrow Color:** Black (#000000).\n*   **Background:** Pure White (#FFFFFF).\n\n**Summary of Visual Logic:**\nThe diagram clearly distinguishes the linear success path (Start -> Receive -> Check -> Yes -> Normalize -> Output -> End) from the failure path (Check -> No -> Reject -> End) using spatial separation (vertical vs. side branch) and standard flowchart geometry (diamonds for decisions, rectangles for actions).",

  "retrievalContext": "Reference 1 (journal_pbio.2003779.g001): The Experimental Design Assistant\nThe Experimental Design Assistant (EDA) workflow.\nThe workflow is not fixed and different users might prefer to do some steps in a different order. A potential workflow using the different functionalities of the EDA is described as follows: (1) The user starts by drawing a diagram (with nodes and links) representing the experiment they are planning. Assistance is provided in the form of examples, templates, and video tutorials. (2) Information is added into the node properties, providing more details about the specific step of the process represented by each node. (3) The “Critique” functionality (see Table 2) enables the researcher to obtain feedback on the diagram and the design it represents. The feedback might prompt a change in their plans or the addition of missing information. This is an iterative process and the user might go through the first 3 steps a number of times. (4) Once feedback from the critique has been addressed and the user is satisfied with the final design, the analysis method suggested by the system can be reviewed (see Table 2). (5) Depending on how the data will be analysed, a suitable sample size can be calculated using one of the calculators provided within the system. (6) Once the number of animals needed per group is known, the EDA can generate the randomisation sequence. The spreadsheet detailing the group allocation for each animal can be sent directly to a third party nominated by the user, thus blinding the allocation. This enables the researcher to remain unaware of the group allocation until the data have been collected and analysed. (7) Diagrams can be safely shared with colleagues and collaborators at any stage of the process. (8) The user can export a PDF report, which contains key information about the internal validity of the experiment, a summary of the feedback from the system, and the EDA diagram itself. This report can be submitted as part of a grant application, as part of the ethical review process, or, later on, with a journal manuscript. Alternatively, the diagram data can be exported (as an.eda file) and saved locally or used to register the protocol before the experiment is conducted. (9) Once the planning is complete, the experiment is carried out. (10) The diagram can be updated after data collection to enable the user to keep an accurate record (e.g., to record the number of animals analysed if some failed to complete the experiment or if data are missing for other reasons).\n{\"figureTypeId\":\"workflow\",\"panels\":[],\"layout\":\"cycle\",\"density\":\"medium\",\"designLessons\":[\"步骤编号与反馈连接结合，区分主要操作和辅助功能。\"],\"doNotTransfer\":[\"案例不是所有实验都必须遵守的唯一流程。\",\"原论文的实体名称、样本、数值、显著性、模型性能与科学结论。\"],\"attribution\":\"Nathalie Percie du Sert, Ian Bamsey, Simon T. Bate, Manuel Berdoy, Robin A. Clark, Innes Cuthill, Derek Fry, Natasha A. Karp, Malcolm Macleod, Lawrence Moon, S. Clare Stanford, Brian Lings. The Experimental Design Assistant. <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 1600 900">
  <defs>
    <marker id="arrowhead" markerWidth="10" markerHeight="7" refX="9" refY="3.5" orient="auto">
      <polygon points="0 0, 10 3.5, 0 7" fill="#000000"/>
    </marker>
  </defs>
  
  <!-- Background -->
  <rect width="1600" height="900" fill="#FFFFFF"/>

  <!-- Styles for text -->
  <style>
    .label-text { font-family: 'Noto Sans', 'Arial', sans-serif; font-weight: bold; fill: #FFFFFF; text-anchor: middle; dominant-baseline: central; }
    .branch-label { font-family: 'Noto Sans', 'Arial', sans-serif; font-size: 16px; fill: #000000; text-anchor: middle; }
  </style>

  <!-- Color Definition -->
  <!-- Teal Green: #1F8A70 -->

  <!-- 1. Start Node -->
  <g transform="translate(800, 80)">
    <!-- Stadium Shape: Rect 200x60 + Circles r=30 -->
    <path d="M -100,-30 L 100,-30 A 30,30 0 0 1 100,30 L -100,30 A 30,30 0 0 1 -100,-30 Z" fill="#1F8A70" stroke="#1F8A70" stroke-width="2"/>
    <text x="0" y="0" class="label-text" font-size="24">Start</text>
  </g>

  <!-- Arrow: Start -> Receive Sample -->
  <line x1="800" y1="110" x2="800" y2="170" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="2" marker-end="url(#arrowhead)"/>

  <!-- 2. Process Block: Receive Sample -->
  <g transform="translate(800, 230)">
    <rect x="-150" y="-40" width="300" height="80" fill="#1F8A70" stroke="#1F8A70" stroke-width="2"/>
    <!-- Icon: Simple Beaker/Test Tube representation -->
    <path d="M -120,-10 L -120,20 L -100,20 L -100,-10 M -115,-10 L -105,-10" stroke="#FFFFFF" stroke-width="2" fill="none"/>
    <text x="0" y="0" class="label-text" font-size="24">Receive sample</text>
  </g>

  <!-- Arrow: Receive Sample -> Quality Check -->
  <line x1="800" y1="270" x2="800" y2="350" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="2" marker-end="url(#arrowhead)"/>

  <!-- 3. Decision Node: Quality Check -->
  <g transform="translate(800, 430)">
    <!-- Diamond Shape -->
    <polygon points="0,-60 120,0 0,60 -120,0" fill="#1F8A70" stroke="#1F8A70" stroke-width="2"/>
    <text x="0" y="0" class="label-text" font-size="22">Quality check</text>
  </g>

  <!-- Branch: Yes (Down) -->
  <!-- Arrow: Quality Check -> Normalize -->
  <line x1="800" y1="490" x2="800" y2="550" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="2" marker-end="url(#arrowhead)"/>
  <text x="815" y="520" class="branch-label">Yes</text>

  <!-- Branch: No (Right) -->
  <!-- Path: Right from Diamond, then Down to Reject -->
  <polyline points="920,430 1100,430 1100,550" fill="none" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="2" marker-end="url(#arrowhead)"/>
  <text x="1010" y="415" class="branch-label">No</text>

  <!-- 4. Process Block: Normalize (Yes Path) -->
  <g transform="translate(800, 610)">
    <rect x="-150" y="-40" width="300" height="80" fill="#1F8A70" stroke="#1F8A70" stroke-width="2"/>
    <!-- Icon: Slider/Graph representation -->
    <path d="M -120,0 L -100,0 M -110,-10 L -110,10 M -80,-15 L -80,15 M -60,-5 L -60,5" stroke="#FFFFFF" stroke-width="2" fill="none"/>
    <text x="0" y="0" class="label-text" font-size="24">Normalize</text>
  </g>

  <!-- Arrow: Normalize -> Output -->
  <line x1="800" y1="650" x2="800" y2="710" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="2" marker-end="url(#arrowhead)"/>

  <!-- 5. Process Block: Output (Yes Path) -->
  <g transform="translate(800, 770)">
    <rect x="-150" y="-40" width="300" height="80" fill="#1F8A70" stroke="#1F8A70" stroke-width="2"/>
    <!-- Icon: Document representation -->
    <path d="M -120,-20 L -80,-20 L -80,20 L -120,20 Z M -115,-15 L -85,-15 M -115,-5 L -85,-5" stroke="#FFFFFF" stroke-width="2" fill="none"/>
    <text x="0" y="0" class="label-text" font-size="24">Output</text>
  </g>

  <!-- Arrow: Output -> End (Left) -->
  <line x1="800" y1="810" x2="800" y2="850" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="2" marker-end="url(#arrowhead)"/>

  <!-- 6. End Node (Left/Center) -->
  <g transform="translate(800, 880)">
    <path d="M -100,-30 L 100,-30 A 30,30 0 0 1 100,30 L -100,30 A 30,30 0 0 1 -100,-30 Z" fill="#1F8A70" stroke="#1F8A70" stroke-width="2"/>
    <text x="0" y="0" class="label-text" font-size="24">End</text>
  </g>

  <!-- 7. Process Block: Reject Sample (No Path) -->
  <g transform="translate(1100, 610)">
    <rect x="-150" y="-40" width="300" height="80" fill="#1F8A70" stroke="#1F8A70" stroke-width="2"/>
    <!-- Icon: Trash/X representation -->
    <path d="M -120,-15 L -100,5 M -100,-15 L -120,5" stroke="#FFFFFF" stroke-width="3" fill="none"/>
    <text x="0" y="0" class="label-text" font-size="24">Reject sample</text>
  </g>

  <!-- Arrow: Reject Sample -> End (Right) -->
  <line x1="1100" y1="650" x2="1100" y2="850" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="2" marker-end="url(#arrowhead)"/>

  <!-- 8. End Node (Right) -->
  <g transform="translate(1100, 880)">
    <path d="M -100,-30 L 100,-30 A 30,30 0 0 1 100,30 L -100,30 A 30,30 0 0 1 -100,-30 Z" fill="#1F8A70" stroke="#1F8A70" stroke-width="2"/>
    <text x="0" y="0" class="label-text" font-size="24">End</text>
  </g>

</svg>
